patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a boxed three-line icon in the top-left, a conventional collapsed navigation trigger.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close the primary navigation menu. The current section should be indicated within the revealed menu.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as an overlay, drawer, dropdown, or inline expansion.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Because the mobile sketch includes a hamburger-triggered collapsed navigation control, keyboard and assistive-tech focus must move predictably when the menu opens and closes.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Focus should move to the opened navigation container or first menu item, and return to the hamburger button when closed. Expanded/collapsed state should be programmatically exposed.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Exact focus target depends on whether the menu is implemented as a drawer, disclosure, or overlay.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a mostly content-driven page with very limited JavaScript needs. The only clear interactive behavior is the mobile-only collapsed navigation represented by the hamburger icon; the desktop sketch instead shows navigation already exposed across the top and a static two-column content layout. No forms, tabs, accordions, modals, pagination triggers, or dynamic loading controls are visibly suggested by either sketch.
